# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old when introduced, later forty-six  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028)</sub>; Mrs.  <sub>[v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a short, dainty woman with thick, snow-white hair that is wavy and styled in curls, puffs, and coils. Underneath her white hair, her face looks girlish and pink-cheeked with wood-brown eyes containing golden glints, dimples, and a sweet-lipped mouth. She wears frilly, delicate, and youthful dresses, such as a cream organdy patterned with pale roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P5](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0005), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is romantic, imaginative, and youthful at heart, loving to play pretend and make-believe as if she were a young girl. Though hospitable, sweet, and sympathetic, she possesses a proud, sulky streak that once ruined her early romance. She enjoys quiet seclusion, loves young people, and admits to a playful fondness for indigestible treats.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P55](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0055), [v2 c21 P62](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0062), [v2 c23 P7](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0007), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)_

- Imaginative and romantic  <sub>[v2 c21 P55](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0055), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar lived isolated at Echo Lodge in Grafton for decades following a broken engagement with Stephen Irving. She maintained a quiet, imaginative lifestyle with her young handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth, playing pretend tea parties and entertaining imaginary companions. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her home, Miss Lavendar formed an instant friendship with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. Soon after, Anne introduced Stephen Irving's young son Paul to her, and the two formed a warm bond. Anne subsequently facilitated a meeting between Stephen and Miss Lavendar when Stephen returned to Prince Edward Island. Resolving their long-standing misunderstanding, Stephen proposed, and the two were married in her garden under the honeysuckle arbor before moving to Boston. They returned to Echo Lodge each summer to vacation and entertain their friends.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P56](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0056), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P34](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0034), [v2 c28 P35](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0035), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Her father named her Lavendar because he fell in love with her mother in a room smelling of lavender  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her father was an English immigrant who built Echo Lodge eighty years ago  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- Was engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years prior, but parted after a foolish quarrel and mutual pride  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Employed a succession of young hired girls from the Bowman family, calling each one Charlotta  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Some are born old maids, some achieve old maidenhood, and some have old maidenhood thrust upon them  <sub>[v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>

> I was determined to be a very nice one. People say I'm odd; but it's just because I follow my own way of being an old maid and refuse to copy the traditional pattern.  <sub>[v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life isn't half as dreadful as it is in books. It's a good deal like a bad tooth . . . though you won't think that a very romantic simile.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
